name: Amber Coast Frontier
inspired_by: The eastern Baltic coast of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania as of 2026: sandy beaches and dunes, pine forest and raised bogs, farmland with timber farmsteads, small towns mixing wooden houses with Soviet-era panel blocks, a port with an LNG terminal and undersea cable landings, and a river border with Russia along the east edge. The real situation is grey-zone pressure (sabotage of cables, drone and airspace incursions, shadow-fleet tankers), not open war; the game's persistent war can escalate it. All towns are fictional.
climate: Humid continental with maritime influence (Koppen Dfb). Summers 18-24 C, long daylight; winters -3 to -10 C with snow cover December-March, sea ice in sheltered bays in cold winters; 600-750 mm precipitation spread through the year; frequent fog on the coast in spring and autumn.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Mar): snow cover, frozen bogs and lakes, short days (6-7 h daylight), icy roads
Spring (Apr-May): thaw and mud (impassable forest tracks), flooding rivers, coastal fog
Summer (Jun-Aug): white nights around midsummer (18 h daylight), dry forests, holidaymakers on beaches
Autumn (Sep-Nov): rain, storms on the coast, early darkness, fog

terrain.relief: Low and gentle: flat coastal plain and dunes (0-20 m), glacial moraine hills and eskers inland (40-120 m), shallow river valleys, large flat bogs. A limestone cliff (klint) 20-40 m high along part of the coast in the north.
features: coastal limestone cliff in the north
a border river with a fortress town on the far bank
dragon's teeth and anti-tank ditch lines near the border (Baltic Defence Line)
terrain.water: Baltic Sea on the west edge with a bay and a port; a border river (60-150 m wide) along the east edge; lakes and bog pools; small rivers and drainage ditches in farmland. Sea ice in sheltered bays in cold winters.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m. Very low-amplitude base; eskers as long sinuous ridges from warped ridged noise; bogs as flat domed patches from a cellular mask; coast via distance field with dune band and, in the north, a cliff step. River border spline on the east edge.
generator.erosion: None needed beyond a light hydraulic pass for ditches and stream valleys.
generator.rivers: Border river spline on the east edge with meanders; small rivers by flow accumulation to the sea; straight drainage ditches in farmland every 150-300 m.
generator.settlement_flattening: Towns and farmsteads flattened lightly (terrain is already flat).
generator.notes: Snow and mud seasons change mobility: bogs freeze and become passable in winter; spring thaw closes forest tracks. Forests limit sightlines to 50-150 m; fields and bogs give long open views.

settlements.architecture: Port town: an old centre of two-storey timber and plastered brick houses with steep tiled or tin roofs, a Lutheran church spire and an Orthodox church with onion domes; Soviet-era five- and nine-storey prefabricated concrete panel blocks on the edge; a harbour with warehouses.
settlements.wall_class: Panel blocks thick concrete (cover); timber houses thin; brick houses medium.
layout_rules: old centre around a market square and church
panel-block microdistrict with courtyards and garages
harbour and industrial strip on the bay

settlements.architecture: Rural villages and farmsteads: one-and-a-half-storey timber houses painted red, yellow or green with steep roofs, saunas, barns of timber or limestone, a former collective-farm (kolkhoz) block of concrete and silicate brick, a shop and bus stop.
settlements.wall_class: Timber thin; limestone barns thick; silicate brick medium.
layout_rules: farmsteads dispersed along roads, each with a tree ring
village core at a crossroads with a shop and church
kolkhoz block and grain dryer on the edge

settlements.architecture: Soviet-era microdistrict of a larger city: nine- to twelve-storey panel blocks around courtyards, schools, a shopping centre, heating plant chimney, garages.
layout_rules: heating plant and garages on the edge

settlements.architecture: Military, energy and infrastructure sites: an allied forward-presence base (barracks, vehicle sheds, training area), a port with an LNG floating terminal, an undersea cable landing station, a border guard station with a fence and towers, bunker and dragon's-teeth defence lines, a radar on a hill.
settlements.wall_class: Concrete bunkers thick; sheds thin; dragon's teeth block vehicles.
layout_rules: base at a town edge with a training area in the forest
border station on the river road
defence line of bunkers and teeth 1-3 km from the border

infrastructure.roads: A coastal highway, two-lane roads between towns, forest gravel tracks and firebreaks; a border bridge (closed) over the river.
infrastructure.rail: Electrified line to the port (European gauge being built beside the old broad-gauge line: Rail Baltica construction site POI).
infrastructure.power: Power lines, an interconnector substation, wind farms offshore and on the coast, a gas pipeline to the LNG terminal.
infrastructure.ports: Commercial port with ferry and container quays, an LNG floating terminal, a naval base, small fishing harbours. LHD standoff in the bay.
infrastructure.airfields: Regional airport and a military airbase inland (out of bounds, AI aircraft).
infrastructure.checkpoints: Border guard station and closed bridge on the east edge; port security gates; military checkpoints only during escalation.

pois.description: Low concrete building with a fenced yard, manholes and a beach duct where undersea data and power cables land; a sabotage target.
pois.contract_use: undersea cable site security; counter-sabotage guard (clients est, lva, ltu, fin, swe)

pois.description: Floating storage and regasification vessel at a jetty, pipelines ashore, a control building, a fence and a coastguard post.
Ageing tanker anchored in the bay suspected of dragging its anchor over cables; crew uncooperative.
pois.contract_use: maritime boarding support for a coastguard (clients fin, est, swe, dnk)

pois.description: Border station on the river road with a fence, cameras, towers, a closed bridge and a fortress-town skyline across the river.
pois.contract_use: border security patrol; drone incursion response

pois.description: Belt of new concrete bunkers, dragon's teeth, anti-tank ditches and pre-cut tree lines in a forest edge near the border.
pois.contract_use: escalation-phase defence; recon of a breach

pois.description: Allied multinational battlegroup base: barracks, vehicle sheds with tanks and IFVs, a fuel point, a helipad, a training area.

pois.description: Crash site of a stray long-range drone in a bog or field, police tape, locals filming.
pois.contract_use: recover sensitive debris before others; secure the site (clients pol, ltu, est)

pois.description: Rail line construction site: embankment, bridge piers over a river, cranes, cabins, stacked rails.
Soviet panel-block courtyard with playgrounds, garages and a heating-pipe trench; an apartment used by a sabotage cell.

pois.description: Radar and observation post on the coastal cliff with a lighthouse, a bunker and a mast.
pois.contract_use: site defence; overwatch for a boarding

pois.description: Hidden cache in a spruce forest near the border: buried containers, a dug-out, trail cameras.
pois.contract_use: locate and recover a sabotage cache (client est or lva)

pois.description: Ferry terminal with linkspan, car queues, passenger hall and parking.
pois.contract_use: VIP or evacuation movement; port security

weather.visibility_notes: Fog and low cloud often ground drones and helicopters; winter darkness from 16:00; white nights in June make NVGs nearly useless; snow shows tracks.

civilians.behaviour: Orderly, low-density towns; commuters 07:00-09:00 and 17:00-18:00; summer beach crowds; mushroom and berry pickers in forests in autumn; hunters in forests. Civilians report suspicious activity to police; on drone alerts they stay indoors. Defence-league volunteers in uniform are not civilians.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Lower density than most theatres, but every casualty is very visible; urban counter-sabotage raids carry high casualty risk.

frontline: Grey-zone by default: the river border does not move. Events from rus (cable damage, drone and airspace incursions, sabotage cells, GPS jamming) raise alert levels in coastal and border zones and post counter-sabotage, site-security and debris-recovery contracts. If the campaign's simulated war escalates (late game, proposed), rus crosses the river and the Baltic Defence Line becomes the front, with allied brigades counter-attacking from their bases. Contracts here are mid-to-late campaign.
contract_hooks: Undersea cable landing station security against a sabotage team (clients est, lva, fin, swe)
Boarding support on a suspect shadow-fleet tanker (clients fin, est, dnk)
Recover drone debris from a bog before others reach it (clients ltu, pol, est)
Counter-sabotage raid on a cell in a panel-block flat (clients lva, est, with police)
Locate and recover a sabotage cache near the border (clients est, lva)
Border security patrol along the river during a provocation (clients est, ltu)
Recover lost NATO equipment from a training area (clients deu, gbr, can)
Escalation scenario: hold a defence-line bunker until the allied QRF arrives (late game)

hot_zones.name: Defence line escalation (late game, fictional what-if)
hot_zones.layout: rus HQ across the river in the fortress town; 4-5 bridgeheads and forest outposts; checkpoints at road junctions; roaming recon and drone teams; 2 QRF bases with armour; allied brigade base as the friendly anchor

insertion.fob: LHD in the bay for coastal contracts; inland FOB at the allied forward-presence base. Roads are good; helicopters limited by fog; AAVs useful on the coast and through bogs only when frozen (proposed).

early_game_notes: Peer-state threat (rus, late tier) in grey-zone form; mid-to-late campaign.
